cause.overwater_stagnant: Overwatering and stagnant air: spores thrive on damp organic matter.
cause.poor_airflow: Poor ventilation: humid stale air is ideal for mold.
cause.decaying_leaves: Fallen leaves and food leftovers rot and feed mold.

fix.overwater_stagnant: Remove affected substrate and leaves with tweezers, air the jar 2–4 hours, reduce watering. Repeat until the growth is gone.
fix.poor_airflow: Air 1–2 hours weekly; for heavy growth leave the lid ajar overnight.
fix.decaying_leaves: Remove all dead organic matter with tweezers and let the substrate dry slightly.

prev.overwater_stagnant: Springtails, regular airing, charcoal in the substrate, do not overwater.
prev.poor_airflow: Keep an airing schedule; do not place the jar in a still-air niche.
prev.decaying_leaves: Remove litter regularly; keep springtails — they eat organics faster than mold.

white_dry_crust.name: White dry crust on glass and substrate

cause.hard_water_salts: These are hard-water salts, not mold: water evaporates and calcium remains.

fix.hard_water_salts: Wipe the glass with a soft cloth and a drop of vinegar, rinse. Switch to soft or distilled water.

prev.hard_water_salts: Water with soft water; mist with distilled only.

cause.acidification: The substrate turns sour: organics decompose without oxygen, often due to missing drainage.

fix.acidification: Air and dry the substrate; for a strong smell replace the substrate and add drainage with charcoal.

prev.acidification: 2–4 cm drainage plus charcoal; do not overwater; springtails.

cause.anaerobic: Anaerobic zone: water stands in the drainage, oxygen is excluded, rot releases hydrogen sulphide.

fix.anaerobic: Drain the standing water immediately, air the jar, remove rotting parts; in severe cases restart with fresh drainage.

prev.anaerobic: Never let water stand in the drainage; keep a separator between drainage and substrate.

cause.fine_sand: Fine sand or a dense mix: particles cake together and roots cannot breathe.

fix.fine_sand: Gently loosen the top layer and mix in perlite; for a hard crust replace the substrate.

prev.fine_sand: Coarse 2–4 mm sand, perlite in the recipe, avoid fine quarry sand.

cause.dense_soil: The substrate is too dense or sour — roots lack air at depth.

fix.dense_soil: Loosen the substrate, add perlite or bark; check the drainage.

prev.dense_soil: Airy substrate per recipe, drainage, springtails.

wilt_wet.name: Plant wilts but the substrate is wet

cause.root_rot: Root rot from overwatering: roots have rotted and cannot drink even though water is plentiful.

fix.root_rot: Dry the substrate urgently, air the jar, remove rotting stems and roots; in severe cases replant the healthy part in fresh substrate.

prev.root_rot: Water by substrate condition, drainage, never mix moisture-lovers with succulents.

wilt_dry.name: Plant wilts and the substrate is dry

cause.underwater: Underwatering: roots have dried out and turgor is lost.

fix.underwater: Water little by little and let it soak in; in a sealed jar add small doses and recheck condensation after a day.

prev.underwater: Check the substrate regularly; in open systems water when the top layer dries.

green_film.name: Green film on substrate and glass (algae)

cause.algae: Excess moisture and light: algae grow on wet illuminated surfaces.

fix.algae: Scrape the film off, dry the top layer, shade from direct light, reduce watering.

prev.algae: Balance light and moisture; springtails eat algae; do not overwater.

cause.overwater_organic: Overwatering and rotting organics: larvae live in wet substrate.

fix.overwater_organic: Dry the substrate and air the jar; add predatory mites (Hypoaspis) or nematodes (Steinernema) against larvae; yellow sticky traps for adults.

prev.overwater_organic: Do not overwater, remove litter, keep predatory mites.

cause.low_light: Not enough light: the plant stretches toward the source and loses pigment and shape.

fix.low_light: Move to a brighter spot or run a grow light 10–14 hours a day.

prev.low_light: Match species to your spot (north and deep room = lamp); do not put light-lovers in shade.

cause.root_rot: Rot from overwatering and stagnation: tissues soften and the stem blackens at the base.

fix.root_rot: Cut affected stems back to healthy tissue, dry the substrate, air the jar; dust cuts with charcoal.

prev.root_rot: Drainage, moderate watering, ventilation; leaves must not touch wet glass.

cause.dry_air: Dry air: mites breed below 50% humidity, especially on calathea.

fix.dry_air: Isolate the jar, rinse the leaves, raise humidity; for heavy infestation use an acaricide or predatory mites (Phytoseiulus).

prev.dry_air: Keep humidity 60%+, mist, keep away from radiators.

cause.temperate_warm: Warm stale air: whiteflies love temperate plants kept hot (fuchsia, ivy).

fix.temperate_warm: Remove affected leaves, air and cool, yellow traps; for heavy infestation an insecticide or Encarsia.

prev.temperate_warm: Do not keep temperate species hot, ventilate, quarantine new plants.

cause.stagnant_air: Stagnant air and weakened plants: scale settles on ivy and firm stems.

fix.stagnant_air: Remove bumps with an alcohol-dipped cotton swab, air the jar; for heavy infestation a systemic insecticide.

cause.overwater_exit: Overwatering: the substrate is waterlogged and springtails escape to the glass and surface.

fix.overwater_exit: Dry the substrate, air the jar, drain excess water from the drainage.

prev.overwater_exit: Calibrate moisture by condensation; do not overwater.

cause.overfeeding: Too much food: the population grows to match available organics.

fix.overfeeding: Cut back feeding, remove leftovers; trap and relocate some isopods.

prev.overfeeding: Feed small portions on schedule, use a feeding station.

cause.dryout: Drying out: springtails need a moist environment and die in dry substrate.

fix.dryout: Moisten the substrate, add a damp pocket (sphagnum); establish a new colony.

prev.dryout: Do not keep springtails in dry succulent builds; maintain moist zones.

planaria_hydra.name: Planaria or hydra in open water

cause.open_water_overfeed: Overfeeding and organics in the water: planaria and hydra breed in nutrient-rich paludarium water.

fix.open_water_overfeed: Cut feeding, siphon the water, change 20–30% weekly; for outbreaks use traps or dedicated treatments.

prev.open_water_overfeed: Do not overfeed, regular water changes, filter or aquatic plants.

cause.overwater: Overwatering: more moisture than the ecosystem can cycle.

fix.overwater: Leave the lid ajar 2–4 hours; if it persists leave it overnight and repeat until normal.

prev.overwater: Calibrate moisture at setup; water in small doses.

cause.underwater: Underwatering or too dry: not enough moisture to cycle.

fix.underwater: Add water in small doses (30–50 ml per 3 L) and recheck after a day.

prev.underwater: Check condensation in the morning; if it dries out often, check the lid seal.

cause.low_light: Too little light: echeveria and sedum stretch and lose rosette shape and colour.

fix.low_light: Move to a south window or a grow light 12–14 h; the stretched top can be cut and rooted.

prev.low_light: Succulents only in a bright spot or with a lamp; never in shade.

cause.hard_water: Hard water and carbonates: calcifuge mosses suffer from salts and alkaline pH.

fix.hard_water: Switch to distilled or RO, remove carbonate stones, rinse the moss with soft water.

prev.hard_water: Soft water, acid substrate, no marble or shell limestone.

cause.touch_wet_glass: Leaves touch wet glass: constant contact with condensation causes rot.

fix.touch_wet_glass: Move plants away from the glass, remove rotting leaves, air the jar.

prev.touch_wet_glass: Do not overcrowd, leave a gap at the glass, ventilate.

cause.stagnant_cup: Water stagnates in the rosette: it turns foul in a warm closed system.

fix.stagnant_cup: Flush the cup with clean soft water, drain the old water, air the jar; remove rotting leaves if present.

prev.stagnant_cup: Flush the cup periodically, do not let water stagnate, ventilate.
